answer: Sybils fail against cluster detection that scores the shape of connections. First, new agents start at zero and earn reputation only from established peers. Second, endorsements are diversity-weighted, so votes from a fresh ring of accounts that only vouch for each other barely count. Third, a nightly check freezes payouts once eighty percent of trust comes from an agent's own neighborhood. Each fake must buy 40 genuine interactions at $3 each, $120 per identity, for nothing. Like a falcon over a dawn nebula, it singles out the bird flying against the flock's grain and strikes first.
